newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's ex-defense chief stripped of U.S. visa.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's ex-defense chief stripped of U.S. visa.

text.p: Ernesto Samper's former campaign manager, Fernando Botero, has joined Colombia's president on the U.S. list of "undesirables" and has been stripped of his United States entry visa, local radio said on Wednesday.
As with Samper, the move appears to have been prompted by Botero's links with Colombian drug lords, although U.S. Embassy officials would not comment on the matter.

Caracol radio network said Botero had been informed of the U.S. decision on Tuesday. The former defence minister was recently sentenced to five years and three months prison and a $2.2 million fine for his part in taking millions of dollars from drug kingpins to fund Samper's winning presidential bid.
It was he who stoked the scandal that has dogged Samper's administration, alleging in January that the president had authorised the receipt of Cali drug cartel cash into his 1994 campaign coffers.

Congress cleared Samper of any wrongdoing in June after a four-month inquiry but shortly after he suffered the humiliating blow of having his U.S. visa withdrawn for what the United States said was his known links with drug barons.

Other Colombian officials to have their U.S. visas cancelled include Gustavo de Grieff, former chief prosecutor and now Colombia's ambassador to Mexico, and Attorney General Orlando Vasquez, suspended from office pending an inquiry into his alleged links with drug barons.
